Package frc.robot.subsystems.shooter

Class Shooter

java.lang.Object
edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.SubsystemBase
frc.robot.subsystems.shooter.Shooter
All Implemented Interfaces:
edu.wpi.first.util.sendable.Sendable, edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Subsystem
public class Shooter extends edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.SubsystemBase
Shooter subsystem â€” two flywheel motors for launch velocity and a servo/motor hood for launch angle.

Responsibilities

  • Accept a stream of AimParams from the aiming pipeline and drive the wheels and hood toward the required setpoints each loop.
  • Expose a tracked(Supplier) trigger so the rest of the system knows when both wheel speed and hood angle are within tolerance.
  • Expose a reverse() command for unjamming.
  • Stop wheels when the robot is disabled.

Speed Control Modes

AimParams can specify two types of output via AimParams.SpeedControl:
  • AimParams.SpeedControl.ProjectileVelocity â€” the desired ball exit speed in m/s, converted internally to wheel RPS by scaling against ShooterConstants.kMaxLinearSpeed.
  • AimParams.SpeedControl.MechanismControl â€” wheel speed in RPS directly (used by ToFAim after calibration with the lookup table).

Recovery Mode

When a ball passes through the shooter, the wheels momentarily decelerate due to the ball's inertia. Recovery mode increases motor output aggressively to pull wheel speed back up before the next ball. It is enabled when the speed error exceeds ShooterConstants.kRecoveryErrorThreshold â€” the same threshold used to detect a "significant drop" in periodic() for the seenBall(double) trigger.

IO Layer

All hardware calls go through ShooterIO:
  • ShooterIOHardware â€” two TalonFX motors for wheels, one for hood.
  • ShooterIOSim â€” simulated motor physics.
Mode is selected in RobotStateMachine at construction time.

  • Method Details

    • periodic

      public void periodic()
      Reads hardware inputs and detects ball passage each loop.

      A ball passing through the shooter causes a brief, sharp drop in wheel velocity. Tracking this event supports the seenBall(double) trigger used to sequence re-loading (if implemented). The drop is detected by comparing actual vs reference speed against ShooterConstants.kShootingErrorDetectionThreshold.

    • shoot

      public edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Command shoot(Supplier<AimParams> paramsSupplier)
      Returns a command that continuously tracks the aim parameters and drives the shooter wheels and hood toward the required setpoints.

      Loop Behavior

      Each loop cycle (20 ms):
      1. Poll paramsSupplier.get() for the latest lead-compensated shot parameters.
      2. If the shot is feasible (status == Possible), compute required wheel speed and hood angle and send them to the IO layer.
      3. If infeasible (out of range or no target), command zero wheel speed so the wheels don't run without a valid target.

      Why Wheels Stop on End (finallyDo)

      When this command ends (trigger released, command interrupted, or auto step expires), the finallyDo block runs: it sets active = false and commands wheel velocity to zero. This prevents the wheels from spinning indefinitely after the driver releases the aim button. If an immediate re-shot is needed, the next shoot(java.util.function.Supplier<frc.robot.aiming.AimParams>) call will ramp the wheels back up â€” the ramp time is minimized by the recovery mode logic.
      Parameters:
      paramsSupplier - called every loop to get the latest AimParams from the pipeline; typically state::aimParams from StateManager

    • reverse

      public edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Command reverse()
      Returns a command that spins the wheels in reverse at ShooterConstants.kReverseVelocity to clear jams. Stops the wheels when the command ends.

      Bound to the driver's right bumper in RobotContainer.

    • tracked

      public edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.button.Trigger tracked(Supplier<AimParams> params)
      Returns a Trigger that is true when the shooter is both active (a shoot(java.util.function.Supplier<frc.robot.aiming.AimParams>) command is running) AND both the wheel speed and hood angle are within tolerance of the current target parameters.

      This is the primary "ready to fire" signal. It is polled by RobotStateMachine.isShootReady() and gates the hopper in ShootWhenReady.

      The active guard prevents a false positive when no shoot command is running (wheels at zero, reference at zero â†’ error at zero â†’ incorrectly "ready").

      Parameters:
      params - supplier of current aim parameters; polled each scheduler tick
